h1: Office space planning for relocations and reconfigurations
lead: BRS organizes space, furniture and functions to work together, so your office makes efficient use of the room you have.
card_blurb: Layouts that match space, furniture and workflow, for new offices, expansions, consolidations and reconfigurations.
meta_description: Space planning that aligns furniture, workgroups and workflow, for relocations, expansions, consolidations and reconfigurations.
overview: Space planning organizes the space, furniture and functions of an office so they work together and meet the needs of your employees and clients.
Whether you are relocating to a new space, expanding or consolidating a facility, or making cosmetic changes, BRS provides practical solutions for efficient use of space.

benefits.title: Efficient use of space
benefits.text: Layouts are built around how your groups actually work.

benefits.title: Fewer surprises later
benefits.text: Planning accounts for building codes, lighting, storage and communication needs up front.

benefits.title: Coordinated execution
benefits.text: BRS also handles moves, furniture and IT coordination, so the plan carries through.

included: Planning around workgroup function and teaming requirements
Review of building codes and regulations
Planning for relocation and design of a new space

process.title: Understand the needs
process.text: We review workgroups, workflow and the constraints of the space.

process.title: Plan the layout
process.text: We organize furniture and functions to fit the space, within code and building requirements.

process.title: Coordinate the change
process.text: Reconfigurations disrupt staff, so we coordinate with IT and facilities to carry out the changes.

who_for: Companies relocating to a new space
Organizations expanding or consolidating a facility
Facilities and IT teams planning a coordinated change

faq.q: What does space planning take into account?
faq.a: Workgroup function, building codes and regulations, lighting, teaming requirements, inter-communication and storage.
They can be complex and disruptive to staff, and involve a chain of events that includes IT and facilities.

faq.q: What types of projects do you plan for?
faq.a: Relocation and design of a new space, expansion or consolidation of an existing facility, and cosmetic enhancements.
